- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.50) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast, targeting 1–2 std dev below recent high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 7–10 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% per day for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underperforms; add 2–4% upward bias to forecast for next 5 days.
